question: Who among the following was the first Gupta ruler of ancient India, married to a Lichchavi princess?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta I 

 
 
• **​Sri Gupta established the Gupta dynasty.**
 
• Through his marriages and conquests, he significantly increased the strength and reputation of his dynasty.
 
• Kumara Devi, a lichchhavi princess, was his wife.
 
• She was the coin's first depiction of an Indian monarch.
 
• The Gupta Era is claimed to have begun under Chandragupta I on February 26, 300 AD, which is also considered to be his coronation day.
 
• He proclaimed himself in charge of Magadha, Saketa, and Prayaga.
 
• The title of Maharajadhiraja** **was first used by him, a Gupta king.
 
• He produced a gold coin that greatly boosted the empire's strength and reputation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Skandagupta**

 
 
• **​Skandagupta was an Indian Gupta emperor.** His **Bhitari pillar** inscription implies that he re-established the Gupta dynasty by vanquishing his adversaries, who might have been rebels or outside invaders.
 
• He repelled an attack by the **Kidarites,** possibly the** Indo-Hephthalites** (also known as Hunas in India).
 
• He is regarded as the final of the great **Gupta Emperors **and appears to have maintained authority over the land he inherited.
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta Vikramaditya**
 
 
• **​**One of the most powerful emperors of the** Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta II, also known by his given name Vikramaditya and as Chandragupta Vikramaditya.** 
 
• Chandragupta carried on his father **Samudragupta's expansionist programme, **primarily by military conquest.
 
 
 
• **Kumaragupta I**
 
 
• **​**In ancient India, **Kumaragupta I reigned as emperor of the Gupta Empire**.
 
• He appears to have retained control over his inherited kingdom, which stretched from Gujarat in the west to the Bengal region in the east. 
 
• He was the child of queen **Dhruvadevi and Gupta emperor Chandragupta II.**
 
• Despite the lack of specific information regarding his military prowess, Kumaragupta carried out an **Ashvamedha sacrifice**, which was often carried out to demonstrate imperial sovereignty.
